headline: OpenAI's Symphony Turns a Project Board into a Coding Factory
lede: A specification from OpenAI called Symphony instructs a long-running daemon to watch a Linear project board, claim eligible issues, and dispatch each to an autonomous Codex agent that will — without human prompting — write code, open pull requests, and mark the ticket done. Released in spring 2026 and quickly accumulating 18,000 GitHub stars, it is less a product than a blueprint: a language-agnostic spec with a reference implementation in Elixir, designed to be copied and reimplemented. Its governing idea is that the right interface for managing AI coding agents is not a chat window but a project board.

concepts.definition: A fast, keyboard-first project management tool built for software teams. Issues move through configurable states (To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done); Symphony uses the Linear API as both its input queue and its durable state store.

An agent execution pattern in which the model iterates in a loop until an external verifier — not the model itself — signals completion. Between iterations, state is stored outside the context window (in files, git commits, or external comments) to prevent degradation across long runs. Named after Ralph Wiggum of The Simpsons by developer Geoffrey Huntley.

A daemon architecture pattern in which a long-running process wakes on a fixed interval (a tick), evaluates system state (the poll), and assigns work to available handlers (the dispatch). Symphony's orchestrator uses this to periodically check Linear for eligible issues and route them to Codex agent workers.

A widely-used AI agent pattern (Reasoning + Acting) in which the model interleaves step-by-step reasoning with tool calls and decides autonomously when the task is complete. Contrasted with Ralph loop, where an external condition — not the model's own judgment — determines exit.

OpenAI's AI coding agent, used by Symphony as the worker subprocess that reads an issue description, writes code in an isolated workspace, and opens pull requests. Symphony spawns one Codex process per Linear issue.

The practice of building modular, deterministic test infrastructure — strict type systems, unit tests, integration harnesses — that allows automated agents to verify their own changes reliably. Analysts identify weak harnesses as the primary reason Symphony underperforms in legacy codebases.

The Erlang virtual machine, capable of running millions of lightweight concurrent processes with low memory overhead. Symphony's Elixir reference implementation uses BEAM to manage dozens of parallel Codex workers efficiently.

repos.summary: Symphony is the subject of this brief: an open-source specification and Elixir reference implementation for orchestrating autonomous Codex coding agents via a Linear project board. The repo contains SPEC.md (the language-agnostic protocol), the Elixir orchestrator daemon, a WORKFLOW.md template system, and configurable lifecycle hooks for workspace setup and teardown.
